subproblem.title: Cylinders over null-measurable sets are null-measurable
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k] and π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) for y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))). Assume (NT): for every N ⊆ ℝ^P with Hᵐ(N) = 0, H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0. Then for every Hᵐ-null-measurable M ⊆ ℝ^P, the cylinder {y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} : π(y) ∈ M} is H^{m+1}-null-measurable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), (∀ N : Set (Eucl P), (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) N = 0 → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0) → ∀ M : Set (Eucl P), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet {y : Eucl (P + 1) | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ M} (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof (null-measurability of {π ∈ M}); the null-set transfer (D1) that the parent derives from (MP) is taken here as the hypothesis (NT).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], equiv_n := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ : Eucl n ≃L[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ); π(y) := equiv_P⁻¹(Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y)) = (y_1, …, y_P) for y ∈ E′. (NT) is the hypothesis: for every N ⊆ E with Hᵐ(N) = 0, H^{m+1}({y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0 (the null-set transfer (D1) of the parent proof).

1. (π is Borel.) π = equiv_P⁻¹ ∘ (f ↦ Fin.tail f) ∘ equiv_{P+1}; every coordinate y ↦ equiv_{P+1}(y)(i.succ) is continuous (continuous_apply), so π is continuous (continuous_pi, continuity of equiv_P⁻¹) and therefore measurable.
2. (π is quasi-measure-preserving from H^{m+1} to Hᵐ.) Let B ⊆ E be Borel with Hᵐ(B) = 0. Then (π_*H^{m+1})(B) = H^{m+1}(π⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply, π measurable, B Borel) = H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ B}) = 0 by (NT). Hence π_*H^{m+1} ≪ Hᵐ (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk), and with Step 1, π is quasi-measure-preserving (Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving π H^{m+1} Hᵐ).
3. (Conclusion.) Since M is Hᵐ-null-measurable there is a Borel set M_B with M =ᵐ[Hᵐ] M_B. Because π is quasi-measure-preserving, π⁻¹(M) =ᵐ[H^{m+1}] π⁻¹(M_B) (QuasiMeasurePreserving.preimage_ae_eq: the set where the indicators of π⁻¹(M) and π⁻¹(M_B) differ is π⁻¹ of the Hᵐ-null set where those of M and M_B differ), and π⁻¹(M_B) is Borel by Step 1. Hence π⁻¹(M) = {y : π(y) ∈ M} is H^{m+1}-null-measurable; this is exactly MeasureTheory.NullMeasurableSet.preimage applied to the quasi-measure-preserving map of Step 2. ∎

  have hπm : Measurable (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) =>
      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y))) := by
    refine ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm.continuous.comp ?_).measurable
    exact continuous_pi fun i =>
      (continuous_apply i.succ).comp (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).continuous
  have hq : Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving (fun y : Eucl (P + 1) =>
      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)))
      (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) := by

    rw [Measure.map_apply hπm hs]
    exact hNT s hs0
  exact hM.preimage hq
proof_key_steps: (NT) on Borel null sets gives π_*H^{m+1} ≪ Hᵐ, so π is quasi-measure-preserving from H^{m+1} to Hᵐ.
Preimages of null-measurable sets under quasi-measure-preserving maps are null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.preimage).

audit.reason: NT is explicitly present in both statements. Continuity of π and NT establish quasi-measure-preservation, which transports null-measurability without additional finiteness assumptions. The proof is complete, non-circular and independently compiled.
